discovery: Discovery of baryon acoustic oscillations in the large-scale distribution of galaxies, establishing a standard ruler for cosmic expansion

nominees.name: Daniel J. Eisenstein
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University / Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian

nominees.name: Will J. Percival
nominees.affiliation: University of Waterloo and Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics

motivation: In 2005, the SDSS team led by Daniel Eisenstein and the 2dF Galaxy Redshift Survey team, including Shaun Cole and Will Percival, independently detected the imprint of primordial sound waves in the clustering of galaxies. That acoustic scale, set in the early-universe plasma, gives a standard ruler that is calibrated by physics, not by astrophysical assumptions. It is geometrically independent of the supernova distance ladder. BAO confirmed cosmic acceleration by a completely separate route, and it became a cornerstone of precision cosmology. Eisenstein's theoretical framework and reconstruction methods, together with Percival's and Cole's analyses, turned it into the key dark-energy probe for BOSS, eBOSS, and now DESI. DESI's 2024-25 results hint that dark energy may evolve. The measurement is now testing the cosmological constant itself, as a precise, independent cross-check should.
